overview: Ethiopia is a landlocked country in the Horn of Africa and one of the most populous countries in Africa. Its capital, Addis Ababa, is the headquarters of the African Union. Ethiopia is one of the oldest countries in the world and was never colonised, apart from a short Italian occupation from 1936 to 1941. It is believed to be the birthplace of coffee.

geography.text: Much of Ethiopia is a high plateau split by the Great Rift Valley, with mountain ranges such as the Simien Mountains. Lake Tana, the source of the Blue Nile, lies in the north-west. The lowlands to the north-east include the Danakil Depression, one of the lowest and hottest places on Earth.

history.text: Ethiopia is one of the oldest countries in the world. The Kingdom of Aksum adopted Christianity in the 300s, and later kings claimed descent from King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba. At the Battle of Adwa in 1896, Ethiopia defeated Italy and stayed independent. Italy occupied it from 1936 to 1941. Emperor Haile Selassie was overthrown in 1974, and a severe famine struck in the 1980s.

events.title: Aksum adopts Christianity
events.text: King Ezana makes Christianity the state religion.

events.title: Lalibela churches
events.text: Churches are carved out of solid rock at Lalibela.

events.title: Nobel Peace Prize
events.text: Abiy Ahmed wins for making peace with Eritrea.

government.text: Ethiopia is a federal parliamentary republic of regional states based largely on ethnicity. Parliament chooses the Prime Minister, who holds most power. A war in the Tigray region from 2020 to 2022 killed hundreds of thousands of people. Addis Ababa is home to the African Union.

economy.text: Ethiopia has one of Africa's fastest-growing economies. Coffee, which originated there, is its biggest export, along with flowers, gold and oilseeds. Ethiopian Airlines is the largest airline in Africa. The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Nile is Africa's biggest hydropower project.

culture.text: Ethiopia has its own calendar, about seven years behind the Western one, and its own script, Ge'ez. It was never fully colonised. Coffee ceremonies and injera, a spongy flatbread, are central to daily life. The rock-hewn churches of Lalibela are a UNESCO site.

items.title: Lalibela
items.text: Eleven churches carved from solid rock.

items.title: Ethiopian calendar
items.text: Thirteen months; New Year is in September.

items.title: Coffee
items.text: Legend says a goatherd discovered it in Ethiopia.

sport.text: Ethiopia is a distance-running superpower. Abebe Bikila won the 1960 Olympic marathon barefoot, the first Olympic gold for a Black African. Haile Gebrselassie, Tirunesh Dibaba and Kenenisa Bekele are among the greatest runners ever.

items.text: Abebe Bikila won the Olympic marathon barefoot in Rome.

items.title: Kenenisa Bekele
items.text: Held the 5,000 m and 10,000 m world records for over 15 years.

didYouKnow: Ethiopia uses its own calendar, about seven years behind the one used in most of the world.
Coffee is thought to have first been discovered in Ethiopia.
